key_facts: Referred to a neurologist 7 months later
Developed progressive right-sided weakness over 3 months
Brain MRI showed hyperintensities in bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas
No contrast enhancement on T1-weighted MRI
Brain biopsy showed CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells
Bone marrow was negative for lymphoma cells

raw.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells, along with the imaging findings of hyperintensities in the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter and other areas without contrast enhancement, are highly suggestive of primary central nervous system lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphomatosis cerebri
rejected.why: Lymphomatosis cerebri is a rare condition and the provided information does not specifically support this diagnosis over primary central nervous system lymphoma.

rejected.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma typically presents with systemic symptoms and the imaging findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy is caused by the JC virus and typically occurs in immunocompromised patients, which is not indicated in the vignette.

rejected.label: Multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: Multiple sclerosis typically presents with discrete episodes of neurological dysfunction and the imaging findings, along with the presence of lymphoma cells, do not support this diagnosis.
